title: Comprehensive Exploration of Synthetic Data Generation: A Survey
authors: Bauer, A.; Trapp, S.; Stenger, M.; Leppich, R.; Kounev, S.; Leznik, M.; Chard, K.; Foster, I.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of 417 synthetic data generation models from the last decade, categorizing them into 20 types and 42 subtypes to guide model selection.
problem_and_motivation: Machine learning progress is hindered by limited training data due to expensive acquisition and privacy laws. Synthetic data generation offers a solution, but the abundance of models and limited overview literature makes model selection difficult for researchers.
approach: Surveyed 417 SDG models from the last decade, identifying 20 distinct model types and 42 subtypes.
Classified models using over ten criteria including generated data types, performance, privacy, and training processes.
Analyzed model performance relationships by tracking which models outperform others across time.
Compiled the most frequently used public datasets and evaluation metrics for SDG models.
Provided a decision-tree-based guideline for selecting appropriate SDG models based on use case.
findings: num: 417 SDG models surveyed and classified into 20 types and 42 subtypes.
Computer vision is the most popular application field, with GANs as the dominant generative model.
Diffusion models, transformers, and RNNs compete with GANs for different generation tasks.
Privacy-preserving SDG remains in early stages, limited to low-dimensional data using simplistic models.
No common standardized evaluation metrics or datasets exist for SDG models.
num: 355 out of 388 models use at least one publicly available dataset.
GANs are compared against 83 times, followed by autoencoders at 62 times.
Newer models generally outperform older ones across all model categories.
key_figures_tables: Figure 59: Decision tree for SDG model selection based on data type and privacy needs → provides practical model selection guidance.
Table 1: Comparison of this survey to prior reviews → shows broader scope with 417 models vs. 13-45 in prior works.
Figure 44: Breakdown of model types by category → GANs dominate at 156 models.

definitions.definition: Synthetic Data Generation - the process of creating artificial data using generative models.
Generative Adversarial Network - a model framework where a generator and discriminator compete.
Variational Autoencoder - an autoencoder that learns a latent probability distribution.
Fréchet Inception Distance - a metric comparing real and generated image distributions.
Negative Log-Likelihood - measures how well a model assigns probability to observed data.
Mean Opinion Score - a human evaluation rating scale for data quality.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides the most comprehensive taxonomy of synthetic data generation models to date, categorizing 417 works into 20 types and 42 subtypes. It reveals key trends including the dominance of GANs, the rise of diffusion models, and the persistent challenge of non-standardized evaluation. The work introduces classification categories for generated data types, performance, privacy considerations, and training processes. A practical decision-tree guideline is provided for model selection based on data type, privacy requirements, and task complexity.
directly_justifies: GANs are the most popular SDG model type with 156 surveyed implementations.
Computer vision is the dominant application field for synthetic data generation.
No common standardized evaluation metric exists for SDG models across domains.
Privacy-preserving SDG is limited to low-dimensional data using simple models.
Newer generative models consistently outperform older ones in comparative evaluations.
limits: Scope restricted to models from the last decade, excluding earlier foundational work.
Survey does not include training/computational cost analysis for most models.
Limited coverage of domain-specific SDG applications outside computer vision.
Evaluation comparability hampered by different metrics and datasets across studies.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 14 (Synthetic Data Generation for Financial ML) was flagged as high relevance since it is the paper's core subject. Domains 4 (Landscape of Existing Systems) and 10 (Data Privacy) received medium relevance for their coverage of generative model landscape and privacy-preserving methods respectively. Domain 12 (Evaluation Frameworks) received medium relevance for its analysis of SDG model evaluation challenges. Domains 1-3 (Filipino Young Professionals, Financial Practices, Expense Categorization), Domain 5-7 (Financial Behavioral Profiles, Predictive Modeling, Budgeting), Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection), Domain 9 (Mobile-First Design), Domain 11 (Engagement Dynamics), and Domain 13 (Savings/Debt Management) were all rejected as they fall outside the paper's scope of synthetic data generation methodology.

limitations: Survey restricted to models from the last ten years, potentially missing foundational approaches.
Training and computational costs are rarely reported in the surveyed literature.
Comparison across models is difficult due to different metrics and datasets used.
Limited coverage of domain-specific SDG applications beyond computer vision.
No original experimental evaluation of SDG models is performed.
